frame_account_level.granularity: ACCOUNT-LEVEL — same across every move (gap: not per-move yet)

frame_permove.granularity: move-level (per-move frame reader; veers measured vs account baseline)

moves.label: M1
moves.paraphrase: The women plus some others arrive at the tomb at daybreak carrying the prepared spices.
moves.outcome: arrival at the tomb with spices
moves.sitz: post-burial visit to a tomb to tend a corpse
moves.paradigm: Jewish burial customs; women's mourning role
moves.gloss: They come as mourners doing what love requires — the burial rites the sabbath had interrupted; the reader meets them not as witnesses to a miracle but as women faithful to a corpse.

moves.label: M2
moves.paraphrase: They discover the stone has been rolled back from the tomb's entrance.
moves.gloss: The sealed threshold is already unsealed before they arrive; something has acted here before them, and the ordinary work of tending the dead is quietly overtaken.

moves.label: M3
moves.paraphrase: They go inside the tomb.
moves.gloss: They cross the threshold anyway — grief keeps its appointment even when the setting has changed under their feet.

moves.label: M4
moves.paraphrase: Inside, they do not find the Lord Jesus' body.
moves.gloss: The absence is registered before it is interpreted; what love came to do cannot be done, and the reader feels the hollow before anyone names it.

moves.label: M5
moves.paraphrase: They become deeply puzzled by the absence.
moves.gloss: The women are not yet given a meaning for what they see — the account lingers honestly in the blank space where an answer should be.

moves.label: M6
moves.paraphrase: Suddenly two men in shining garments are standing beside them.

lineage.seam: Is the pair of men in dazzling clothing standing on the Danielic angelophany type-scene, and if so does the revelatory-interpreter role of t

moves.gloss: Into the blank space something breaks in from outside — the source of understanding is no longer the women's own looking but a word arriving from beyond them.

moves.label: M7
moves.paraphrase: The women become terrified.
moves.substrate: the appearance of the two men
moves.gloss: The right response to a heavenly presence is not curiosity but dread; the fear itself is a form of accurate recognition.

moves.label: M8
moves.paraphrase: They bow their faces down to the ground.
moves.substrate: their own faces / to the earth
moves.gloss: The body knows what the mind has not yet caught up to — bowing enacts the acknowledgment that something greater than them is standing there.

moves.label: M9
moves.paraphrase: The two men address the women with a question.
moves.sitz: angelic address at the empty tomb
moves.gloss: The heavenly figures do not merely announce; they engage — the women are addressed as ones capable of being spoken to and answering back.

moves.label: M10
moves.paraphrase: They challenge the women for looking for a living one where the dead lie.
moves.sitz: angelic interpretation of the empty tomb
moves.gloss: The question is really a correction: they are looking in the wrong category, and their expectation itself is what needs to be reset.

moves.label: M11
moves.paraphrase: They declare that he is not present here but has been raised.
moves.gloss: The absence is finally given its meaning from above — what looked like loss is announced as something wholly new that has been done to him.

moves.label: M12
moves.paraphrase: They tell the women to recall what he said back in Galilee.
moves.substrate: the women's memory / his prior words
moves.sitz: angelic prompt to recollect prior teaching
moves.gloss: The new event is anchored to a word already spoken — they are not asked to believe on the spot but to bring an earlier teaching back to mind.

moves.label: M13
moves.paraphrase: Jesus, back in Galilee, told them beforehand what would happen to the Son of Man.
moves.narrator: the two men, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: The teaching being invoked belongs to him — his own prior words become the frame through which today's emptiness is to be read.

moves.label: M14
moves.paraphrase: The content foretold: the Son of Man must be handed over to sinful men, be crucified, and on the third day rise again.
moves.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — the Son of Man as patient
moves.outcome: handed over, crucified, and raised on the third day
moves.sitz: prophetic necessity in Jesus' Galilean teaching
moves.narrator: the two men quoting Jesus, via the narrator

lineage.seam: Is the 'third day' rising formula standing on Hosea's 'on the third day he will raise us up,' and if so does the corporate covenantal reviva
Is the divine-passive 'must be handed over to sinful men' standing on the Servant who was 'handed over' for the iniquity of others, and if s
imports the Danielic 'Son of Man' title as the subject of a passion-and-resurrection prediction, but leaves unsaid whether the exalted heave

moves.gloss: The pattern he laid down — handed over, killed, raised — is presented not as accident but as something that had to unfold this way.

moves.label: M15
moves.paraphrase: The women call his earlier words to mind.
moves.gloss: The recognition happens inwardly first: the past teaching clicks into place and reframes the present without anyone having to argue it to them.

moves.label: M16
moves.paraphrase: The women head back from the tomb.
moves.gloss: Understanding turns immediately into motion — a private insight becomes an errand back to the community.

moves.label: M17
moves.paraphrase: They report everything that happened to the eleven and to the rest of the followers.
moves.substrate: the eleven and all the rest
moves.outcome: the events reported to the group
moves.sitz: first witness-report of the empty tomb
moves.gloss: The women are the first to carry the news; the account places the announcement of the resurrection in their mouths before anyone else's.

moves.label: M18
moves.paraphrase: The narrator identifies the women as Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary mother of James, and other women with them.
moves.gloss: The narrator pauses to name them — not anonymous mourners but particular, identifiable people whose word can be checked.

moves.label: M19
moves.paraphrase: The other women with them likewise report these things to the apostles.
moves.outcome: the events reported to the apostles
moves.gloss: The report is not one voice but many — the message is corroborated within the women's own circle before it ever reaches the men.

moves.label: M20
moves.paraphrase: The words strike the hearers as idle nonsense.
moves.gloss: The hearers hear the words as empty chatter; the message is present but the room is closed against it.

moves.label: M21
moves.paraphrase: They refuse to believe the women.
moves.gloss: The refusal deepens from dismissal into flat unbelief — the women are trusted messengers to a community that will not receive them.

moves.label: M22
moves.paraphrase: Peter, however, gets up and runs off to the tomb.
moves.gloss: One hearer at least is unsettled enough to check — disbelief in the room does not fully cover a private need to see.

moves.label: M23
moves.paraphrase: Bending down to look inside, he sees the linen wrappings lying by themselves.
moves.substrate: the strips of linen (in the tomb)
moves.outcome: observation of the linens lying alone
moves.gloss: He looks with his own eyes and sees only the leftover cloths — the physical evidence is real but partial, less than an appearance.

moves.label: M24
moves.paraphrase: He leaves and heads home.
moves.gloss: He leaves with less than he came for — the evidence did not resolve into a meaning, and the tomb sends him home unfinished.

moves.label: M25
moves.paraphrase: He puzzles over what has taken place.
moves.gloss: The wondering is left uncompleted on purpose — the account refuses to hand Peter the recognition that will belong to others.

moves.label: M26
moves.paraphrase: That same day, two of the group are traveling to a village called Emmaus, about sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
moves.substrate: the village Emmaus (destination; sixty stadia from Jerusalem)
moves.gloss: The next scene starts elsewhere and moves outward — Jerusalem's unresolved report becomes the freight two travelers carry down the road.

moves.label: M27
moves.paraphrase: They discuss with each other everything that has just happened.
moves.substrate: all these things that had happened
moves.gloss: Two people trying to sort out what happened by talking it through — the ordinary human work of trying to make grief make sense.

moves.label: M28
moves.paraphrase: As they talk and question each other, Jesus himself draws near.
moves.gloss: The one they are talking about steps into their conversation — the shift is quiet, but the source of what they can now know is no longer only their own memories.

moves.label: M29
moves.paraphrase: He walks along with them.
moves.gloss: He joins their walking rather than announcing himself — a companion on the road before he is anything else.

moves.label: M30
moves.paraphrase: Their eyes are held so that they cannot recognize him.
moves.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — their eyes as patient
moves.substrate: the two travelers' recognition of Jesus
moves.sitz: concealed identity of the risen Jesus
moves.gloss: The disclosure is deliberately held back — recognition is not something they can seize but something that has to be given at the right moment.

moves.label: M31
moves.paraphrase: Jesus asks the two travelers what they are discussing as they walk along looking sad.
moves.sitz: encounter on the road to Emmaus
moves.gloss: He begins as any stranger might — with a question that opens a conversation rather than an announcement that closes one.

moves.label: M32
moves.paraphrase: He asks them what topic they are exchanging with each other while walking, noting their sadness.
moves.substrate: the two travelers' conversation and their sadness
moves.gloss: The question notices what the walk itself was showing — that they were carrying something heavy in their bodies as they went.

moves.label: M33
moves.paraphrase: One of them, Cleopas by name, replies to him.
moves.gloss: One of them steps forward by name, giving the exchange a particular voice the reader can hold onto.

moves.label: M34
moves.paraphrase: Cleopas asks — with surprise — whether Jesus is the only visitor in Jerusalem who has not learned what has been happening lately there.
moves.substrate: Jesus' apparent ignorance of recent Jerusalem events
moves.sitz: road encounter; assumption that the events are common knowledge
moves.paradigm: public notoriety of the passion events
moves.gloss: The events feel so public to Cleopas that only a stranger could have missed them — the irony is that the one asking IS the events.

moves.label: M35
moves.paraphrase: Jesus asks them back which things they mean.
moves.gloss: He declines to fill in the answer for them — the story has to come out of their own mouths before he can give it back to them differently.

moves.label: M36
moves.paraphrase: He asks which things they are referring to.
moves.gloss: He gives them the room to say it in their own words, letting their account of the events take shape without prompting.

moves.label: M37
moves.paraphrase: They reply to him.
moves.gloss: They take up the invitation to speak — the road becomes the place where their version of the story gets told aloud.

moves.label: M38
moves.paraphrase: They point to the matters concerning Jesus of Nazareth.
moves.outcome: topic named as Jesus the Nazarene
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: They give the story its subject: everything now circles around one person and what happened to him.

moves.label: M39
moves.paraphrase: They characterize Jesus as a prophet powerful in deed and word before God and all the people.
moves.sitz: public reputation of Jesus prior to the passion
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: Their summary is admiring but past-tense — he was a great prophet, and that framing is exactly what the following days broke.

moves.label: M40
moves.paraphrase: They report that the chief priests and their own rulers handed Jesus over for a death sentence.
moves.agent: the chief priests and our rulers
moves.outcome: handed over to be condemned to death
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: They name the machinery of his death plainly — their own leadership handed him over; the wound is inside the house.

moves.label: M41
moves.paraphrase: They report that those same authorities crucified him.
moves.agent: the chief priests and our rulers
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: The mode of death is not softened — the specific horror of crucifixion is what is being carried in their grief.

moves.label: M42
moves.paraphrase: They confess they had been hoping he was the one to redeem Israel.
moves.substrate: Jesus as the awaited redeemer of Israel
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator

lineage.seam: Is the hope of one who would 'redeem Israel' standing on the Deutero-Isaianic language of YHWH as Israel's redeemer, and if so does the divi

moves.gloss: The rawest line: they had staked a hope on him, and speak now from the far side of that hope collapsing.

moves.label: M43
moves.paraphrase: They note that on top of everything else, this is now the third day since these events took place.
moves.sitz: reckoning of days since the crucifixion
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: Reciting the day-count is a way of measuring how long the silence has held — three days without the reversal they had been taught to expect.

moves.label: M44
moves.paraphrase: They add that some women of their group astonished them, having gone to the tomb at early morning.
moves.agent: certain women of our company (having arrived early at the tomb)
moves.sitz: reception of the women's tomb-report inside the travelers' circle
moves.paradigm: astonishing witness of the empty tomb
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: The women's report enters their own account as one more unsettling piece — received, but not yet trusted enough to change anything.

moves.label: M45
moves.paraphrase: The women did not find his body at the tomb.
moves.sitz: the women's tomb-report as retold on the road
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: The absent body is passed along as the women's finding — a fact the travelers can repeat but not interpret.

moves.label: M46
moves.paraphrase: The women returned and reported what they had seen.
moves.sitz: women's testimony recounted on the road
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: The chain of witness gets one more link: they are quoting women who were quoting what they had seen.

moves.label: M47
moves.paraphrase: They claimed to have seen a vision of angels.
moves.narrator: the women (twice-nested: via the travelers via the narrator)
moves.gloss: The angelic sighting is repeated as claim rather than owned as certainty — the travelers place it at arm's length as "what the women said."

moves.label: M48
moves.paraphrase: The angels said he was alive.
moves.narrator: the angels (thrice-nested via women via travelers via narrator)
moves.gloss: The core announcement is repeated in the travelers' summary — the message survives the retelling even where belief does not.

moves.label: M49
moves.paraphrase: He is alive.
moves.gloss: The claim in its barest form — three words that the whole account is trying to teach them how to receive.

moves.label: M50
moves.paraphrase: Some of their own group then went to the tomb themselves.
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: Other members of the group followed up — the report was taken seriously enough to be checked, even if not yet believed.

moves.label: M51
moves.paraphrase: They found conditions matching the women's description.
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: The tomb's physical state matched the women's account — the men's investigation confirmed the women were not making it up.

moves.label: M52
moves.paraphrase: But they did not see Jesus himself.
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: Corroboration reached the tomb but not the person — the men could verify the emptiness but not the one who had left it empty.

moves.label: M53
moves.paraphrase: Jesus responds to them.
moves.sitz: road encounter — Jesus' rebuke and instruction
moves.gloss: He picks up the conversation from inside their account — no announcement, just a response that takes their words seriously enough to answer.

moves.label: M54
moves.paraphrase: He calls them dull-minded and slow at heart to trust everything the prophets said.
moves.outcome: the travelers named foolish and slow-hearted
moves.gloss: The problem, he tells them, was never lack of evidence — it was a heart too slow to trust the scriptures they already knew.

moves.label: M55
moves.paraphrase: He asks rhetorically whether the Christ was not obliged to suffer these things and then enter his glory.
moves.substrate: the necessity of the Christ's suffering-then-glory pattern

lineage.seam: imports the Servant's necessary suffering as warrant for the Christ's suffering-then-glory pattern, but leaves unsaid whether Isaiah's Serva

moves.gloss: The suffering they had experienced as the collapse of the hope was, all along, the shape the hope was supposed to take.

moves.label: M56
moves.paraphrase: Starting with Moses and running through all the prophets, he interprets to them all the scriptural passages that speak of himself.
moves.substrate: all the scriptures (from Moses and the prophets onward) concerning himself

lineage.source_ref: Moses and all the Prophets (Torah + Nevi'im, unspecified loci)
lineage.seam: imports the whole of Moses-and-the-Prophets as a christologically-referring corpus, but leaves unsaid WHICH passages and by what hermeneutic

moves.gloss: He walks them through their own scriptures with him as the key — the texts they knew are reopened around a center they had not seen.

moves.label: M57
moves.paraphrase: They approach the village they are heading for.
moves.gloss: The teaching has ended and the village is here — the road-conversation reaches its natural stopping point.

moves.label: M58
moves.paraphrase: He gives the appearance of intending to travel farther.
moves.gloss: He does not force his company — the decisive moment is placed inside their freedom to invite him or let him pass.

moves.label: M59
moves.paraphrase: They press him to stay.
moves.gloss: Their pressing is the small opening the whole scene has been waiting for — hospitality is what lets the recognition happen.

moves.label: M60
moves.paraphrase: They ask him to remain with them because it is nearly evening and the day is almost gone.
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: The reason they give is ordinary — it's getting dark — and the ordinariness is the point: the extraordinary enters through everyday care for a stranger.

moves.label: M61
moves.paraphrase: He enters to remain with them.
moves.gloss: The invitation is accepted; the guest who might have gone past becomes a guest inside a house.

moves.label: M62
moves.paraphrase: He reclines at table with them.
moves.substrate: the table with the two travelers
moves.sitz: evening meal at the Emmaus village
moves.gloss: The stranger they invited in takes his place at their table — the shared meal opens the space where recognition can happen.

moves.label: M63
moves.paraphrase: He takes the loaf into his hands.

lineage.seam: imports the standard Jewish take–bless–break–give host sequence as the vehicle of recognition, but leaves unsaid whether the ordinary domest

moves.gloss: The guest quietly assumes the host's role — his hands take the bread, and the arrangement of the meal shifts.

moves.label: M64
moves.paraphrase: He gives thanks over it.
moves.substrate: the bread (implicit; blessing said over it)
moves.gloss: The blessing is Jewish and ordinary — the recognition to come will hinge on a gesture any Jewish table would recognize.

moves.label: M65
moves.paraphrase: He breaks the bread.
moves.gloss: The bread is broken in the same fourfold sequence they had seen him do before — the shape of the action is what carries the memory.

moves.label: M66
moves.paraphrase: He hands it to them.
moves.outcome: bread handed to the two travelers
moves.gloss: The bread passes from his hands to theirs — the sequence completes in the giving, which is where the moment turns.

moves.label: M67
moves.paraphrase: Their eyes are opened.
moves.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — their eyes as patient

lineage.seam: Is the divine-passive 'their eyes were opened' at a shared meal standing on Eden's 'the eyes of both were opened' after eating, and if so do

moves.gloss: What had been held closed is now opened for them; the seeing is granted, not achieved.

moves.label: M68
moves.paraphrase: They recognize him.
moves.gloss: The face across the table is suddenly known — the person they had walked and eaten with resolves into who he actually is.

moves.label: M69
moves.paraphrase: He becomes invisible to them.
moves.outcome: Jesus no longer visible to them
moves.gloss: In the same instant, he is no longer there — the recognition is complete, and his visible presence is withdrawn precisely at that fullness.

moves.label: M70
moves.paraphrase: They speak to each other.
moves.gloss: The reflex is immediate speech — they need to say to each other what has just happened.

moves.label: M71
moves.paraphrase: They ask each other, in retrospect, whether their hearts were not on fire inside them while he was speaking on the road and opening the scriptures.
moves.substrate: the traveling encounter and scriptural opening
moves.outcome: realization that they had been inwardly kindled
moves.sitz: retrospective recognition of the on-road experience
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: Looking back, they realize the recognition had already been happening in their bodies while he spoke — the heart knew before the eyes did.

moves.label: M72
moves.paraphrase: They stand up at that very hour.
moves.outcome: on their feet, ready to move
moves.gloss: Recognition instantly becomes urgency — the meal is left, the evening ignored; the news cannot wait until morning.

moves.label: M73
moves.paraphrase: They travel back to Jerusalem.
moves.gloss: The retreat from Jerusalem reverses — the same road that carried them away in grief now carries them back with something to say.

moves.label: M74
moves.paraphrase: They find the eleven together with those in their company.
moves.substrate: the eleven and those with them
moves.gloss: They arrive to find the community assembled and waiting — the isolated experience is about to enter a shared one.

moves.label: M75
moves.paraphrase: The gathered group is already declaring the news to them.
moves.agent: the eleven and those with them
moves.gloss: Before they can speak, they are being spoken to — the news is already breaking out from more than one source at once.

moves.label: M76
moves.paraphrase: They declare that the Lord has truly been raised.
moves.agent: the eleven and those with them
moves.outcome: assertion that he is truly risen
moves.narrator: the eleven and company, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: The proclamation now comes out of the community's shared mouth — no longer one witness's claim but the group's confession.

moves.label: M77
moves.paraphrase: They report that he has appeared to Simon.
moves.agent: the eleven and those with them
moves.narrator: the eleven and company, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: A particular appearance to a named leader is attached to the general claim — the news is being anchored in specific people it happened to.

moves.label: M78
moves.paraphrase: The two travelers narrate what happened on the road.
moves.gloss: The Emmaus travelers now add their own strand — first-person testimony joining the pile of others' reports.

moves.label: M79
moves.paraphrase: They report how he was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
moves.substrate: the recognition-event at the breaking of the bread
moves.outcome: account of how Jesus was recognized delivered
moves.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
moves.gloss: They give the recognition its distinctive shape — it happened at the breaking of the bread, and that specificity is what they hand to the community.

moves.label: M80
moves.paraphrase: While they are still telling this, Jesus himself is standing in their midst.
moves.outcome: Jesus present in the middle of them
moves.gloss: The testimony has barely landed when the one testified to is himself in the room — the reports are overtaken by the person they were about.

moves.label: M81
moves.paraphrase: He addresses them.
moves.sitz: first words of the risen Jesus to the group

lineage.seam: Is the 'Peace to you' greeting standing on the Tanakh's shalom-formula (often spoken to reassure a terrified recipient of a theophany), and

moves.gloss: He speaks first — the room does not have to figure out what to do; the initiative comes from him.

moves.label: M82
moves.paraphrase: He bestows peace on them.
moves.gloss: The first word he gives is peace — not proof, not rebuke, but the gift of steadiness offered before anything else.

moves.label: M83
moves.paraphrase: The group is thrown into terror and fear.
moves.gloss: The peace does not land — the actual response to a real appearance is not calm but panic.

moves.label: M84
moves.paraphrase: They suppose that what they are seeing is a ghost.
moves.outcome: belief that they are seeing a spirit
moves.sitz: first-century ghost/spirit construal of an apparition
moves.gloss: They reach for the category they have — a ghost — because a visible dead person fits nothing else they know.

moves.label: M85
moves.paraphrase: What they are seeing is a spirit.
moves.narrator: the group (as their supposition), reported by the narrator
moves.gloss: The supposition names itself: whatever this is, it belongs to the world of shades, not to the world of bodies.

moves.label: M86
moves.paraphrase: He addresses them.
moves.gloss: He answers the misperception by speaking to it directly — the ghost-hypothesis is not left to fade but is met head-on.

moves.label: M87
moves.paraphrase: He asks why they are agitated.
moves.sitz: reassurance in the middle of terror
moves.gloss: The question puts their fear back to them as a problem to be examined rather than a mood to be indulged.

moves.label: M88
moves.paraphrase: He asks why doubts are welling up in their hearts.
moves.substrate: the doubts arising in their hearts
moves.outcome: challenge posed to their inner doubting
moves.gloss: The doubt is treated as a real thing rising inside them — he names the inner motion instead of pretending it isn't there.

moves.label: M89
moves.paraphrase: He commands them to look at his hands and his feet to confirm his identity.
moves.substrate: the group's sight of his hands and feet
moves.gloss: He offers his wounded hands and feet as the proof — the marks of the crucifixion are exactly what shows this is the same person.

moves.label: M90
moves.paraphrase: He commands them to touch him and see for themselves.
moves.gloss: Looking is not enough; he invites their hands as well — the proof he offers is willing to be pressed and tested.

moves.label: M91
moves.paraphrase: He argues that a spirit does not have flesh and bones such as they can see he has.
moves.gloss: He rules out the ghost category on its own terms — whatever a spirit is, it isn't this thing you can see and touch.

moves.label: M92
moves.paraphrase: Having said this, he shows them his hands and feet.
moves.gloss: Words are backed with the thing itself — his hands and feet are shown so the argument doesn't have to be trusted, only seen.

moves.label: M93
moves.paraphrase: They still cannot believe it, out of joy, and remain amazed.
moves.outcome: state of joyous disbelief and wonder
moves.gloss: The failure to believe here is not resistance but overflow — the good news is too much to take in all at once.

moves.label: M94
moves.paraphrase: He addresses them again.
moves.gloss: Speech restarts the interaction — even the joy that is stopping them has to be moved through, not around.

moves.label: M95
moves.paraphrase: He asks whether they have any food on hand.
moves.gloss: He asks for food as a person would — the request itself is meant to close the last gap between what they are seeing and what they can believe.

moves.label: M96
moves.paraphrase: They hand him a piece of grilled fish and some honeycomb.
moves.substrate: a piece of broiled fish and some honeycomb
moves.gloss: They respond with what they have on hand — the exchange becomes as ordinary as a shared supper.

moves.label: M97
moves.paraphrase: He takes the food from them.
moves.gloss: His hand receives what theirs offers — the giving-and-taking is itself a proof no argument could match.

moves.label: M98
moves.paraphrase: He eats it in their sight.
moves.gloss: He eats in front of them — the plainest possible demonstration that the body they are looking at can do what bodies do.

moves.label: M99
moves.paraphrase: He speaks to them once more.
moves.gloss: With the ghost-question settled, the exchange turns to teaching — now that they can believe he is here, he can begin to say what it means.

moves.label: M100
moves.paraphrase: He reminds them that while still with them he had told them everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must come to fulfillment.
moves.substrate: his prior teaching about scriptural-fulfillment concerning himself
moves.outcome: reminder that all Law-Prophets-Psalms passages about him must be fulfilled

lineage.source_ref: Law of Moses + Prophets + Psalms (tripartite Tanakh)
lineage.seam: imports the tripartite Tanakh (Torah / Nevi'im / Ketuvim-headed-by-Psalms) as a single corpus that must be fulfilled in him, but leaves unsa

moves.gloss: He anchors the present moment to earlier words — everything happening now had already been laid out in what they knew.

moves.label: M101
moves.paraphrase: He opens up their minds so they can grasp the scriptures.
moves.outcome: minds opened to understand the scriptures
moves.gloss: Understanding here is given, not achieved — he does something to their minds so the scriptures can finally be read.

moves.label: M102
moves.paraphrase: He addresses them.
moves.gloss: With their understanding opened, he begins to say what it now lets them hear — the illumination is followed by the teaching it was for.

moves.label: M103
moves.paraphrase: He points to what stands written.
moves.gloss: He points them to the written word as the settled ground — what happened had to happen because it stands there in writing.

moves.label: M104
moves.paraphrase: It was necessary that the Christ suffer and rise from the dead on the third day.
moves.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — the Christ as patient
moves.outcome: suffered and raised on the third day

lineage.seam: imports the Servant's necessary suffering and Hosea's third-day rising as scriptural warrant for the Christ's death-and-resurrection pattern

moves.gloss: The suffering and the rising are laid down together as one required pattern — the cross is not the exception to the plan but the shape of it.

moves.label: M105
moves.paraphrase: Repentance and forgiveness of sins are to be proclaimed in his name to every nation, starting from Jerusalem.
moves.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — content to be proclaimed
moves.substrate: repentance and forgiveness of sins in his name
moves.outcome: proclamation to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem
moves.move_type: proclamation (missional mandate embedded in the necessity)

lineage.seam: imports the Isaianic vision of a message going out from Zion to the nations as warrant for a Jerusalem-originating proclamation of repentanc

moves.gloss: What has happened to him is meant to travel — the private events of one Jewish week become an announcement aimed at every people.

moves.label: M106
moves.paraphrase: He designates them as witnesses of these things.
moves.gloss: Their status shifts from bystanders to witnesses — being present at these things becomes a role they now have to carry.

moves.label: M107
moves.paraphrase: He announces that he is sending upon them what his Father promised.
moves.outcome: the Father's promise sent upon them
moves.sitz: promise of what the Father has pledged
moves.gloss: The commission comes with a promised gift — they are not being sent on their own strength, and the sending waits on what will be given.

moves.label: M108
moves.paraphrase: He commands them to remain in the city until they are clothed with power from on high.
moves.substrate: the group's remaining in Jerusalem until they are clothed with power from on high
moves.sitz: instruction to stay in Jerusalem until endowed with power

lineage.seam: imports Joel's promise of the Spirit poured out on all flesh as the 'Father's promise' / 'power from on high,' but leaves unsaid whether Joe

moves.gloss: Until the promise arrives, the right posture is stillness — the mission begins with waiting rather than doing.

moves.label: M109
moves.paraphrase: He leads them out as far as Bethany.
moves.substrate: the group (led as far as Bethany)
moves.outcome: the group brought out to the vicinity of Bethany
moves.sitz: leaving Jerusalem for the ascension site
moves.gloss: He takes them out to the edge of the city — the setting of the parting is chosen, not incidental.

moves.label: M110
moves.paraphrase: He raises his hands.

lineage.seam: Is the lifting of the hands to bless standing on the Aaronic priestly gesture of Leviticus 9, and if so does an Aaronic priestly benediction

moves.gloss: Hands raised over a gathered people is the priest's posture — what he is about to do is meant to be seen as blessing, in the old temple sense.

moves.label: M111
moves.paraphrase: He blesses them.
moves.gloss: The last thing he does to them is bless them — the goodbye is shaped as a gift rather than a farewell.

moves.label: M112
moves.paraphrase: As the blessing goes on, he departs from them.
moves.gloss: The blessing is not interrupted by the leaving — the parting happens inside the giving, so what he was doing to them is what remains.

moves.label: M113
moves.paraphrase: He is taken up into heaven.

lineage.seam: Is the divine-passive being-carried-up-into-heaven standing on Elijah's ascent, and if so does an Elijah-type translation get repurposed as

moves.gloss: He goes up, and the direction is theological as much as physical — the one who was handed down and killed is now lifted up into God's own place.

moves.label: M114
moves.paraphrase: They worship him.
moves.gloss: They give him what only God is given — the response to the ascension names what they now understand him to be.

moves.label: M115
moves.paraphrase: They return to Jerusalem with great joy.
moves.outcome: return to Jerusalem accomplished, with great joy
moves.gloss: They walk back the way they came, and the mood of the return is the opposite of what left Jerusalem earlier — joy where there had been grief.

moves.label: M116
moves.paraphrase: They stay continually present in the temple.
moves.sitz: post-ascension habitual gathering at the Jerusalem temple
moves.gloss: The joy settles into a place — the temple becomes their habitual home, and the resurrection community begins in the old house of prayer.

moves.label: M117
moves.paraphrase: They keep praising God.
moves.gloss: Praise becomes their steady work — the response to what has happened is not a single act but a continuing life.

moves.label: M118
moves.paraphrase: They keep blessing God.
moves.gloss: Alongside praise, blessing — the Jewish grammar of thanks to God stays the native language of this new community.

moves.label: M119
moves.paraphrase: An affirming closing word seals the account.
moves.gloss: The account signs itself off with a settled Amen — the reader is left inside the affirmation, not on the outside looking at a claim.
